They are all squawking and talking loudly. Mithu goes mad inside his cage, which Reeti has now placed near the window. He squawks, he jumps up and down and spreads his wings. Reeti watches. “Are they your friends, Mithu?” she asks. Mithu doesn’t answer. He only looks at the parrots on the tree. As swiftly as they had come, the parrots fly away. “What were they saying, Mithu?” Reeti asks. “Hello,” says Mithu sadly. “Hello.” Reeti’s holidays are over. It is the first day of school. Reeti meets all her friends and teachers. During the lunch break she plays happily with her friends. The big trees around the school playground are full of twittering birds. When Reeti reaches home after school, she sees Mithu sitting quietly in his cage. “Hello, Mithu,” she whispers. He looks at her but doesn’t say anything. Reeti puts down her schoolbag. She opens the window. Then she opens the door of the cage. “Go, Mithu!” she says. “Go and find your friends.” He looks at her. “Go, Mithu!” she says again. “Fly away!” Mithu steps out of his cage. He looks at Reeti one last time. And with a final “hello”, he spreads his wings and flies away to join his friends. WHO NEEDS A PET? Anyone who wants a loving and loyal friend needs a pet. If you're feeling lonely and lost or mean and mad, a pet is sure to do something... anything to make you glad. A pet will play with you, make you feel better, teach you lots of important things, and bring endless fun into your life. Now, who doesn't want that? SHOULD YOU HAVE A PET OR NOT? Sure, pets are fun, but don’t rush out to get one! Think carefully: - Will your parents let you keep a pet? - Do you really want a pet? Remember, a pet is for life. It is not a toy you can throw away once you get bored with it. - Pets need food, clean water, exercise, and love. They also have to be trained, taken to the vet, and given baths. That means extra work, every single day. Do you have the time for that? - Can you forgive your pet if it makes a mess with its muddy paws, or chews your favourite shoes? AM I REALLY READY FOR A PET? Your best friend has a pet, and you wish you had one too! So you’re wondering whether you should get a dog, a cat, or maybe, even a rat. Stop right there, before you pick a pet, and ask yourself these questions. Do I have the time to take care of a pet? Having a pet is a h-u-g-e responsibility. Whether it is for training, feeding or plain loving, you’ve got to spend time on your pet – big time! Do I have space at home for a pet? Small pets like cats, fish and birds can adapt to houses of any size. But dogs may need more space to run around and exercise. What kind of pet do I want? If you want a specific kind of pet, talk to a vet or to people who own similar pets. Find out what they eat and how they behave. Then think hard about whether the pet will suit you. Can I afford to have a pet? All pets require food and shelter. Then, there are the visits to the vet for check-ups, vaccinations, and for treatment when the pet falls ill. Will a pet be welcome at home? You may love animals, but do the rest of the family share your feelings? You need to talk this through with your family before you get a pet.
level_3.author: Anupa Lal

level_1.title: The Cut Hair
level_1.Text: She runs very fast. Sometimes, Kia looked back to see if her mother and grandmother were still chasing her. She is always afraid every time she gets her hair cut. For Kia, cutting her hair is scary. After she ran far, she arrived at aunt Maya's house. She looked at Oren sitting looking at the twilight sky. Kia stands up beside Oren and does the same. Kia still feels afraid. She is Afraid of scissors touching her beautiful hair. From the kitchen, Aunt Maya greeted Kia gently. She knew why Kia had come here now that her grandmother had called her to tell her. Aunt gently touched Kia's head. Meanwhile, Kia says that she doesn't want to cut her hair. "Why you don't want to cut your hair?" said Aunt Maya after they were in the living room. "I am afraid, Aunt," said Kia in a slow voice. "Afraid? Afraid for what?" said Aunt Maya amazed. "I am afraid of scissors," said Kia softly. Her Aunt glared in shock. "Tell me why you are so afraid of scissors," said Aunt Maya. "I think scissors are like the head of a dinosaur that can swallow me," Aunt Maya smiled. Then Aunt Maya tells Kia that she must not be fearless with scissors. Scissors can not move if they don't move by a human. And scissors are different from a dinosaur which has teeth. Kia nods her head to show she understands. Kia promised after she went from Maya's house, she would ask her mother and grandmother to cut her hair which gets longer. She didn't want to bother with her long hair. Before she goes home, Kia gets a watermelon as a gift from Aunt Maya.
level_1.author: merry  debby

level_1.title: The Decieving Night
level_1.Text: It was a cold and dark night. Paul was still exhilarated after his best friend’s birthday party. Paul was on his way back home when he saw a shadow of a tall and bulk man following him. A chill ran down his spine. Could he be a thief? He walked quicker and tried to find a spot to hide. The man behind him was walking faster as well. Paul was so frightened and about to shout for help when a hand patted on his shoulder. “Don’t be afraid, you’ve dropped your wallet.” The man handed over a wallet to Paul.

level_1.title: The scary night on the jungle trip
level_1.Text: Beep! Beep! the school bus is riding all the way down to the jungle on a school trip. Children are super excited for the trip. Talking about the fun they will have there makes them even more excited. All of a sudden Rinki told what if we see a ghost there, or wild animals attack us? All the children started laughing, just then Rah ul stood up and said that I would like to see who is more scarier than my older sister.The children brust into laughter But Minki who was Rinki 's best friend supported her " Students get off we reached the picnic spot" said the teacher. Hurray! we finally reached here. There was an amazing smile on everyone's face expect Rinki. Minki noticed her sitting under a tree getting worried, she went near her and comforted her. Then they both started playing. At night while sleeping Rinki heard some strange noise. She called Minki and told her the same. Minki waked up and stretched her arms saying "What happened Rinki why are you not sleeping " to this Rinki said " Dear I heard some strange noise. They grabbed the torch and went in search. Unfortunately no one was there. So they decided to move apart in two direction. While walking Rinki suddenly....... Shouted " Ghost! Ghost some body help. Minki ran to that direction and found Rinki crying and screaming with fear. But to her surprise one was there. She comforted Rinki and they both went to the resting place. While returning to their bed they found Rahul was missing. They thought he might have went to the washroom and went to their bed to sleep. In the morning Rinki & Minki told ma'am everything about last night. So the teacher and students went on searching for clues of the last night incident. Suddenly one of the student shouted loudly ma'ammmmmmmmmmmm! come here quickly and look. To every one 's surprise they found a ghost costume under Rahul 's bed. Suddenly Minki remembered she told the teacher that last night while returning they found Rahul 's bed was empty & told her that he might have taken the get up of the ghost to scare Rinki. The teacher was angry and scolded Rahul. Rahul explained that he wanted to use Rinki 's fear for troubling her. He also told sorry to Rinki & Minki. " I am so sorry I am really ashamed of my behavior ". Then Rinki told him not to make such scary noise or scare her in the night ever again. But every one was surprise when Rahul told that he had intended to scare her but failed because he had to go to the washroom. He didn't scare Rinki at the night or herd her crying and screaming. Then who was the ghost Rinki saw last night. Was Rahul lying again. Who was the one made that sound. Did Rinki saw a real ghost. If yes why did Minki found no one there???? Still remained a mystery.

level_1.title: The Haunted Railway Station
level_1.Text: People stopped using the station because they thought it was haunted. Even Indian Railways listed it as haunted in their records. The station was built in 1960. Lachan Kumari, a Santal queen, worked with Indian Railways to set it up. At first, the station was important to local people. But ghost stories changed how people saw it. This shows how rumors can change the way people use public places. Begunkodar station in Purulia district gained fame in 1967. Indian Railways listed it among 10 haunted railway stations after passengers abandoned it. Reports claimed that the station master died after seeing a woman in a white saree walking on the tracks. The railway administration initially dismissed rumors about Begunkodar station. However, the mysterious deaths of the station master and his family fueled public fear. These deaths transformed rumors into reality. Station employees refused to work due to safety concerns. Trains stopped halting at Begunkodar railway station due to staff shortages. The railway authorities attempted to deploy new employees for the next few months. Their efforts failed as no one agreed to work at the railway station. Because of on going staffing issues, officials finally closed Begunkodar station. This closure reinforced local beliefs about the station’s supernatural reputation. The sequence of events demonstrates how rumors combined with unexplained incidents can impact public perception and operational decisions. The station remained closed for 42 years. Mamata Banerjee reopened it in 2009 during her tenure as railways minister. However, fear persisted, and no one stayed at the station after 5 PM. This atmosphere of fear fueled a thriving ‘ghost tourism’ industry. Urban youth often challenged themselves to spend a night at the supposedly haunted station.

level_2.title: Shh! What's That?
level_2.Text: “Good night Dia. Good night Tara!” Dada turns off the light. Fliff! Swish! What was that? Tara looks at Dia. Dia looks at Tara. “Monster!” Dia and Tara hide under their blanket. “What are we going to do?” says Dia. Clunk! Uff! “Let’s scare it away,” Tara says. “With a monster of our own,” says Dia. “The scarf-inator!” “Who has a football head.” “I think we scared it,” Tara says. “Oh no, it’s getting up!” Dia hides. Yaa! Aiyo! “Quick, get your sheet,” Dia says. “We’ll make a sheet-osaur!” “Where is the torch?” Tara asks. Dia points at the street light. Flump Flump! “And I’ll use the torch to make a chair-acabra with my raincoat,” Dia says. “Two monsters should scare it away,” Tara says. “Move the torch close. We’ll make chair-acabra bigger!” Shump Boof! Tara waves her hands under her sheet. Clish! Creaaak! “What are you both doing?” Dada says. “ You are the monster?” Tara and Dia yell. “What monster?” Click! Blink! Ha ha! Hoo hoo! They all laugh and make shadow monsters.
level_2.author: Sanjana  Kapur

level_2.title: The Three Doof-Doofs
level_2.Text: What is that? What is that doof-doof-doof noise? A cat? A mouse? A visitor in the house? No, it’s something even furrier than a cat, even cuter than a mouse, and much tinier than you and me. It’s the three Doof-Doofs. These sweet creatures have only one foot each to hop on. And each hop makes a thumping doof-doof on the floor. AHHHH UHHH! Here is Solly Doof, the smart one, who is always thinking looooong and loud. He uhhs and ahhs and doof-doofs all night long. He reads daytime stories to the other Doof-Doofs, because unlike you and me, that is when they sleep. Thinky, stinky Solly Doof prefers reading over bathing any time. And here is Sally Doof, the smallest and sweetest Doof-Doof of the three. In a little quiet voice, she sings doobee-doobee Doof-Doof songs, when it gets a bit too quiet in the night. She likes finding shiny things and cuddles. Snuggly, huggly Sally Doof who loves to sing. Clink C lank Clunk! Don’t forget Silly Doof, the funniest Doof-Doof in the house. He is always joking. Hahahahaha! Wiggly, giggly Silly Doof will make you laugh until your tummy hurts. He cheers up the other Doof-Doofs whenever they feel sad. He loves to dance on his big silly foot, to the songs that Sally Doof sings. So, if at night you ever hear a strange doof-doof noise again, remember, it’s just the three Doof-Doofs, reading, singing and dancing on their one doof-doof foot. So sleep well, little one. Or keep one eye open... Because maybe, just maybe, you’ll see three cute little creatures hopping past on one foot, going doof-doof-doof.
level_2.author: Claudi  Potter; Wynand Botha

level_2.title: I Need to Hide!
level_2.Text: I love the most? Having a best friend like Na. She takes me home for New Year’s. Na knows that I don’t want to break, so she is very careful. I am always with my best friend Na. Every day, Na feeds me with a bit of her allowance. It’s been one year. The taller Na is, the heavier I am. The new year is coming soon. “The piggy bank is getting heavy. Let’s break it to buy a new dress for Na," Mom says. Na helps me to hide quickly! I will just hide here quietly. Until the end of the day. Oh no! Mom is going to throw the box I'm in on the garbage truck! What should I do? What scares me the most? I decide to make a move. I jump out of the box... Just as I hear Na cry, “don’t throw the piggy bank away!” What’s going to happen? Will I ever see Na again? I open my eyes slowly. "Ah, I can still see things!" Now there is a lovely tree on my back. What do I love the most? Having a best friend like Na. What scares me the most? Not being with her.
level_2.author: Magdalena  Cooper

level_2.title: Lost in the Dark
level_2.Text: Rebone were friends. One day, they went to the forest to fetch firewood. On the way home, they came across a river. They played and played until the forest turned dark. It was so dark that they could not find their way back home. Suddenly, they heard a loud howling from somewhere in the forest. Lebo screamed and ran. The others followed. Then Bonolo shouted, “Hey, look! I see a cave. Let’s hide here.” “No,” said Lebo, “There might be wild animals inside.” All three girls kept running. “Look over there,” pointed Rebone. “I can see lights. Maybe that’s where our home is.” The three girls followed the lights, but soon realised that they had been chasing fireflies. By now the girls were tired and hungry. They decided to rest under a tree. “Come on,” said Lebo. “Let’s climb the tree. We’ll be safer there.” All at once they heard voices and a dog barking. People were calling out their names. Their parents and people from the village had come looking for them. “Here we are!” shouted the girls. The girls were happy to be reunited with their family. They promised never to lose track of time again.
level_2.author: Alisha Berger

level_2.title: Plasto
level_2.Text: Plastic Is Everywhere! Plasto tells us that our misuse of plastic has grown into a big problem. Plastics are polluting our lands, oceans and air. Our bodies too. Plastic has many uses in our day-to-day life. It can save lives, like in hospitals or in rescue missions. But not all plastic is good. By saying no to use-and-throw plastic cups, plates, forks, spoons, etc., each one of us can make a big difference. Plasto, the plastic-greedy monster, will stop growing if we practise the 4 Rs: reduce, reuse, recycle and refuse.
level_2.author: Aithihya Ashok Kumar

level_2.title: Good Night, Monu
level_2.Text: It is bedtime and Monu wishes the world “Good night!” He hugs Amma, he kisses Appa, “Sweet dreams!” he says, “ Sleep tight!” “Good nigh t, Monu.” He sends a kiss to every star, And to the clouds, birds and trees. He sends a wish to each flower, And to every buzzing bee. “Sleep tight,” he says, to the shelf on the wall, And his books lined up in a row. “Rest well,” he says, to the pots and the pans, And the clothes hanging by the door. “Good night, Monu.” “Sweet dreams,” Monu says, to the windows, To the walls, the ceiling, the floor. “Cuddle up,” he smiles, as he tucks in his toys, And “good night,” at last, to… Oh! “Settle down,” Monu says to the monsters, As he puts each one to bed. “Close your eyes! Go to sleep!” he says, as he leaves A kiss on each monster head. “Sweet dreams,” he says, to the whole wide world. “And sweetest dreams to me.” “Good night, Monu.”
level_2.author: Lavanya Karthik

level_2.title: Khuavang
level_2.Text: It was like any other day in 3C. Dari and Kimi were enjoying their book amidst the chatter in the classroom. Suddenly, everything stopped. The tap, tap, tap of the pencils. The screech, screech, screech of the chairs. The rustle, rustle, rustle of shoes. All the sounds seemed to have suddenly disappeared. Even the sunlight felt different, as though the sun itself had paused. An eerie silence spread across the room, and Dari felt her heart quicken. “What is going on?” she thought to herself. She turned to Kimi. Kimi’s eyes were wide. Soundlessly, her mouth moved, and she whispered out the words. “It’s a khuavang kal lai.” Dari’s eyes widened. She had heard of the khuavangs once — strange creatures her grandmother had once told her about. “When there is a moment of complete silence, the khuavangs are believed to walk among us, unseen but present.” “What is a khuavang?” Dari had asked. “They are creatures of nature, you see. You can’t see them, but you can feel their presence. When there is pin-drop silence, almost like magic, that is when you know it is khuavang kal lai,” grandmother had said. Was she going to get a glimpse of the khuavang today? In the suffocating stillness, Dari’s eyes began to wander. Maybe they were really, really big, taking up all the space in the classroom. Or maybe they are very, very small, which is why they cannot be seen. “Could they be sitting on Kimi’s head?” Maybe they liked to fly in the air. Maybe that was why it was so dim. Or maybe, they prefer the ground, silently crawling through all the stillness. With every passing second, Dari’s heart quickened. Is that a flicker? Was that a spot up there? Should she make a sound? What if they heard her? Cough, cough, cough! Gasp! Someone coughed at the back of the class, and then the class was alive again. Tap, tap, tap. Screech, screech, screech. Rustle, rustle, rustle. Dari let out a deep breath. “That was scary, wasn’t it?” Kimi said. Dari nodded as she looked at the boy who had just coughed. A shiver went down her spine. Right there on his forehead was a small, round, dark mole. It had not been there earlier. “Looks like he’s been marked. That’s the khuavang chhinchhiah,” Kimi said in a low voice. “Marked?” Dari asked. “That’s right,” Kimi said. “He was the first to break the silence, so they left him with a little mark. It’s not a bad thing, really, just a little reminder from the khuavangs to honour their stillness.” “Hmmm, a reminder.” Dari whispered. Was the khuavang real, or had she just imagined the whole thing? Either way, she now knew that the silence of the khuavangs should be honoured. Just as she sat, ready to get back to her book, something caught her eye. Right on top of her left hand sat a clear round black mole. She too had received the khuavang’s mark. About the Story In Mizo folklore, the Khuavangs are mythical creatures believed to be unseen but ever-present, especially during moments of unnatural stillness. They are often associated with controlling nature or possessing magical powers. They are typically seen as benign and even benevolent, blessing humans with fertility, a long life, and prosperity. Khuavang Kal Lai is a term from Mizo folklore meaning ‘pin-drop silence’, it refers to a moment when the Khuavangs are near, and the world around falls completely silent. It is said to happen when the Khuavangs walk among humans, and the silence is an indication of their presence. Khuavang Chhinchhiah or the ‘mark of the Khuavang’ manifests as a small, dark mole or mark on a person’s body. It is believed to appear when someone has been touched by the Khuavang, particularly after they have broken the silence caused by their presence. level_2.title: The Name is Grey
level_2.Text: “Cloak and dagger man?” asked Clunch. “My name is Grey, Parma Grey,” I replied, “like a mouse’s back, and I have a cloak, incarnadine in hue, but, alas, no dagger.” He gave that queer, lopsided grin of his. “Ah, Mr Grey, immortalised throughout our fair islands. Do come in.” I followed Clunch into a blue pavilion. The Ministry of Covert Warfare’s idea of keeping a low profile. “Hardly immortalized, I’m supposed to be a secret agent!” Clunch gave a throat-clearing splutter as he pressed a lift button. “Ah, but immortalized amongst we secret people, the cognoscenti of the garotte and poisoned umbrella!” I tried to suppress a smug smile as the lift proceeded downwards. The door opened onto a long corridor and we entered the first room on our left, where I was to be given a briefing on my mission. A huge bald man sat in a huge chair behind a huge desk. His name, appropriately, was Hugo. Hugo Mann. “Mr Clunch, please bring Mr Grey the latest assortment of, er, gadgets.” Things had moved on since the days of Aston Martin ejector seats and boats that could take off and fly. Now it was all microelectronics, miniature cameras and bio-weapons. But there was still time for what I called ‘fun things.’ Umbrellas that could blow a hole in someone and phones that could burn people’s hands off. So, I was shown a range of new gadgets, amongst which I rather took a fancy to a laser pen. Innocuous-looking but with enough power to fry an enemy’s eyeballs. “Be sure to keep the safety catch in the ‘on’ position,” exhorted Clunch. Then there was what appeared to be an ammonite, an ﻿ ancient fossil in two halves, but which had been impregnated with a special kind of plutonium. “Quite harmless,” said Clunch, “but put the two halves together for sixty seconds and … well, you’ll need a fast car to get out of range!” “You mean …?” “Yes.” Finally, clutching a briefcase with enough firepower to start – and finish – a small war, I found myself seated and facing the enormous Mr. Mann again. Surely there was some diet he could go on, I thought. “No there isn’t,” he said, as if having read my mind. “It’s a genetic thing.” Genetic thing my arse. I’d bet he liked his doughnuts soaked in double cream. He laughed. ““And brandy. Well, Parma,” he said, jabbing a finger in my direction, “your mission is to wipe out the Taliban.” ﻿ “With pleasure,” I exclaimed, “the uneducated swine!” “You’ll be parachuting into Kabul tomorrow morning.” “Couldn’t I just go by passenger plane, y’know, incognito?” Mr Hugo Mann’s expansive pink face took on a shiny, sweaty hue. “Hmm. That’d mean getting you a ticket.” “Blimey. Surely the Ministry could manage that!” “Well, er, I suppose so, if you really don’t want to parachute.” “Um, I’d rather not,” I said. “You know, there are a lot of insects floating around up above the desert. I don’t fancy a mouthful of flying earwig.” He stood up, with difficulty, and reached out a huge sweaty paw. “Good luck, Parma, the country, and indeed the world, is depending ﻿ on you!” I shook his hand and surreptitiously wiped the grease off on a handkerchief. “Lead on, Mr Clunch,” I cried, “Afghanistan here I come!”
level_2.author: AGRIM SHARMA

level_3.title: Junuka and the Rice Rakshasas
level_3.Text: Junuka is visiting her Anaideo's* village during the holidays. She has decided to grow some rice for her school project. "Be careful of the rice rakshasas," Anaideo tells her. Everyone in the village is afraid of the rice rakshasas. *'Anaideo' means grandmother in Assamese. But Junuka is not afraid. Junuka must plough the field before she sows the rice seeds. "This will take all day. I wish I had some help," she thinks. Suddenly, she senses something creeping towards her... KHAS KHAS KHAS "AAAAAA!" shouts Junuka. "Rice rakshasa!" The rakshasa flashes its claws and... "Aha! Your soil is ready for planting." SCRATCH SCRATCH SCRATCH SCRATCH SCRATCH SCRATCH "I'm Trakshasur," says the rice rakshasa. "Climb on, I'll help you sow the seeds." Junuka thinks for a minute. Then she climbs on Trakshasur's back. He carries her as she scatters the seeds. They flood the field with water. Over time, the seeds become seedlings. "Time to move them to the big field," says Trakshasur. Junuka pulls out the seedlings and Trakshasur bundles them up. Now they go to get the big field ready. Trakshasur ploughs the big field and Junuka floods it. The soil becomes soft, muddy and ready for planting. Then Junuka hears a slimy, wet sound... "SLLUUUUUURRP!" "AAAAAA!" shouts Junuka. "Rice Rakshasa!" "This is Plantasur. She will help us plant," says Trakshasur. Plantasur picks up the seedlings with her long, red tongue. She bites the mud. She plants dozens of seedlings with every bite. Soon the field is full of seedlings. Junuka puts up scarecrows to protect the seedlings. The rice grains bloom and soon it is harvest time. Junuka hears a sound in the bushes... DRRRRRRRRRRRRRR "AAAAAA!" shouts Junuka. "Rice rakshasa!" "This is Harvasur. She will help us harvest," Plantasur tells her. THWACK! CRUNCH! THOOO! Harvasur cuts the crop, traps the stem and spits out the straw. Until there is a mountain of grain. "Now we must remove the husk from the grain," says Harvasur. "Come, let's visit our friend Dhanasur at the mill." They find Dhanasur in a dark corner of the mill. He's a rakshasa with two heads. "Hello," says Junuka. "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!" shouts Dhanasur. "A human child!" "This is Junuka. You have to help her," says Harvasur. Dhanasur opens one mouth wide and Junuka pours rice into it. Finally, they have shiny, white rice. That night, there is a harvest feast at the village. Junuka brings the rakshasas with her. Junuka shows the villagers all the rice they harvested together. "The rakshasas only want to help us," she says. BURRRRRRRRRRRRP! Junuka has a great time at the feast. And so do the rice rakshasas! Machines used in rice farming Rice farming is a long and difficult process. But with the help of her four friends, Junuka can grow rice easily. Just like the four rakshasas, these machines make farming quicker and easier: Mechanical plough Like Trakshasur, this machine helps farmers to loosen and prepare the soil for sowing rice seeds. Rice transplanter Like Plantasur, this machine helps the farmer plant rice seedlings. Combine harvester Like Harvasur, this machine cuts the crop, collects it and separates the stems from the rice grains. Rice husker Like Dhanasur, this machine removes the brown husk from the grain to give us white rice.
level_3.author: Preeti Hatibarua; Priyadarshini Gogoi

level_3.title: Leech!
level_3.Text: There were only two things that Shanbor enjoyed doing– bossing around and lazing away. “Yaaaawwnnn!! Another day to watch over my people working!” While he loved bossing around, he enjoyed lazing around even more. So lazy was he that he didn't even want to go to his paddy field to supervise his workers. "Let me take a peek through my window." “Are they even working? I can’t see. Yaawnnn. I don't want to go and check now. Maybe tomorrow.” "Maybe tomorrow," he said. And he said this everyday! Then one fine day, Shanbor thought of a BRILLIANT idea! “Aha! I just know what to do! I am so so smart!” “Hello Ding Ding and Mon Mon! I have an important job for you two.” “Go watch over my fields and workers for me. Report everything to me in the evening. Don’t be late!” As Ding Ding and Mon Mon left, Shanbor went back to sleep. “ Now I can go back to sleep. Ding Ding and Mon Mon will do all the work. They will be back in the evening.” As Shanbor snored away to glory, Ding Ding and Mon Mon began their adventures. “Ding Ding, let’s go look for the tallest tree to climb!!” “Mon Mon, this one here is the tallest!” “No, Ding Ding, that one over there is the tallest!” "Adididi! Adadada! Aninini! Hurry Mon Mon, I can't keep an eye on your side of things!" “We have to be diligent and report everything to Master!” “M-mm-master, we are back.” “Ding Ding! Mon Mon! What took you both so long? Report everything to your Master, now!” “Yes, yes Master!” Pleased that he can sleep all day, everyday, Shanbor puts Ding Ding and Mon Mon back. “Time to get back inside, Mon Mon, Ding Ding!” The same cycle continued everyday. One fine day as Mon Mon and Ding Ding were watching over their Master’s fields… …a crow comes and swoops them up… “ Masterrrrrrrrr…!! HELLLPPP!!” …and flies away! As the sun went down and it got darker, Shanbor started wondering where Ding Ding and Mon Mon were. “I can’t see anything! Why are Ding Ding and Mon Mon not back??” A few days passed by and Shanbor managed to crawl out of his house into the dark night. So deep into the night it was that everyone was shut up in their houses. There was no one to help him! “Water! Water! Somebody give me some water!” “Thirsty... I am so thirsty! Maybe I can quench my thirst if I suck my own blood.” “Somebody! Anybody! Deliver me from this misery!!” It seemed like someone had heard Shanbor’s plea. He was turned into... a LEECH! Activity Shanbor is thirsty! Could you guide Shanbor to the water source to quench his thirst?

level_3.title: The Spooky Night
level_3.Text: ﻿ ﻿Story Description Henry and his friends go out one evening to the abandoned park and find a demolished house. They encounter something strange. Pre-Reading Vocabulary and Phonics Abandoned a-ban-dun-d The children found the abandoned house by the park. Unravel un-rav-ul They unravel led the chain for the swings. Shrieked sh-ree-k-d The children shrieked when they heard a scary sound. Vampire v-am-pie-ur A bunch of vampire bats suddenly flew past. "Henry, where have you taken us?" said Gareth. "I'm sure we're not supposed to be here." "Chill out," said Henry. "Don't be such a baby! It's just the park." "This is the abandoned park, isn't it?" said Mary. "We're not allowed to play here." "It's not abandoned," said Henry. "It's just that nobody comes here anymore. We must be the first people in years to visit." "The people in the town said to never go to the abandoned park," said Gareth. "It's haunted." "It is not haunted," said Henry. "Ghosts are not even real. I know because I've never seen one. Come on, let's have some fun." "Well, it can't be that bad," said Mary. "Perhaps Henry is right. We can play here after all. It's not dangerous." Gareth still wasn't sure, but he followed Henry anyway. The children soon found a slide and swing set. The swing was wrapped around the metal pole, as if it hadn't been used in years. "Come on, I'll race you to the swings," said Henry. "Great idea," said Gareth. "Whoever loses has to unravel the chain." "I'm going to beat both of you to it!" said Mary, spreading her arms and running. "Look at the moon," said Mary. The children gasped. "It isn't usually that big," said Henry. "It must be a super moon," said Gareth. "That is when the moon is at its closest distance to the earth, so it looks bigger in the sky." "I don't remember it being so hazy," said Mary. The children continued to play around the swings and slide, dancing, singing songs and telling stories into the night. It was nearly home time, but Henry convinced the children to stay. Henry looked up at the moon and saw clouds pass over. But the moon did not go behind the clouds. It was in front of the clouds. Henry felt something was wrong. "Ooh, this is the abandoned house," said Henry, taking the children past the park to a new area. "Henry, this is bad," said Gareth. "We are definitely not allowed to be here. It could be dangerous." "Relax," said Henry. "Why be scared of some old ruins?" "If we don't go home now, we'll all be in trouble. And we won't be allowed to play together again." Henry ignored Gareth and started investigating through the ruins. Gareth waited near the house, too scared to go inside. Henry found a hammer and started bashing the ground. "Hey, I've found something," he said, hitting a hard metal object. "I think it's an old fashioned safe. There might be money inside. Gareth, give me some help!" But Gareth did not reply. "Gareth? Where are you?" Suddenly, a white sheet with holes appeared. "Oooooh!" it said. "Go away! Go away!" "Ghost!" Henry shrieked. He dropped the hammer and covered his eyes with the fright. Suddenly a cluster of vampire bats flew past, making a huge shadow creep across the ruins. "No!" cried Henry, thinking the bats were going to attack him. "Gareth, get me out of here!" Gareth came and dragged Henry out by the hand, and everyone went home. The next day, Henry told the story to the rest of his friends. He explained about the safe and then seeing the ghost and the vampire bats. "I thought my life was in danger," said Henry. "I was very brave." "No, you weren't," said Mary. "I saw the fright in your eyes." "What?" "The ghost - it was me wearing a sheet," said Mary. "But what about the moon?" said Henry. Nobody could answer. Post-Reading Questions Whose idea was it to go to the abandoned park? What did the children notice about the moon? Re-read page 9. Ask: What did Gareth advise Henry not to do? Re-read page 11. Ask: What did Henry see at the abandoned house? ﻿Re-read page 13. Ask: ﻿What did Mary confess? ﻿What do you think about the children going to the park?﻿

level_3.title: Those were the days...
level_3.Text: 24 March 2015 Dear Diary, Today, I have completed 16 years of adventures, 16 years of blissful and joyous moments and 16 amazing revolutions around the bright sun! I wanted to share with you an experience that has been strange yet fun. ……….……….……….……….……….……….………….……….……….……….……….….. The school near the outskirts of the town looked so scary in the evening, na? When I saw it for the first time, I was with Appa, walking to explore the beautiful scenes of that place. But the school was the thorn of the rose. The place is a dense jungle, and in the middle of the jungle, lies the way to go to the abandoned school. It has been abandoned for years and now the school is a spot for ghostly spirits to live. And, if it wasn’t so difficult to guess, it is actually haunted. Yesterday I heard Appa and uncle talking about the same. Appa said that the school is haunted by a ghostly spirit of the History teacher of that school. It is a very popular tale that one morning the people of our locality, including Appa, found the body of that old fogey lying halfway across the library. Some say it was a heart attack, but no one really knows what had happened the night before. Anyway, Appa said that his last wish was not fulfilled and hence his atript atma (dissatisfied spirit) is still roaming inside the school. By the way, his last wish was something next to impossible, it was building a Taj Mahal similar to the one far in Agra, here in Kazhakkoottam. I mean, what an old fogey he was! He was probably the most hated teacher in history, as he used to live in the subject he used to teach, HISTORY! Now this conversation was all what I heard from the window of our house, when Amma was cooking delicious Rasam for me on the occasion of my birthday. 24 March 2015 Dear Diary, Today, I have completed 16 years of adventures, 16 years of blissful and joyous moments and 16 amazing revolutions around the bright sun! I had a brilliant plan going on in my mind, the time to execute it was in the evening. The evening was full of celebration and glamour, it was the birthday of the only son of the tehsildar of Kazhakkoottam. All my friends had come, in new and beautiful clothes. Gopi and Bhola were also cordially invited, as they are my best friends. After having food, we decided to have some fun. Gopi is the most talkative girl of our class, but today she was talking at a different pace. She was explaining her relation with the most popular subject of our school, HISTORY! She said, "Oh my Goodness! How I wonder can there be any subject as boring as history? What’s really the point of learning something which is of no use in the present?" I argued, as a part of the plan, “But, Gopi, we learn from our roots, our past…” “I am not opposing that buddy, but what do you learn from that boring master. He teaches history as if he has to rush somewhere by the train in the morning, I mean it doesn’t feel like learning. History should be taught like a story, like drama, like an emotion, like a tale, like a…” “Ok, ok I got your point.” I mean, what an old fogey he was! He was probably the most hated teacher in history, as he used to live in the subject he used to teach, HISTORY! Now all this conversation was what I heard from the window of our house, when Amma was cooking delicious Rasam for me on the occasion of my birthday. I had a brilliant plan going on in my mind, the time to execute it was in the evening. Today's evening was that of shine and glamour, it was the birthday of the only son of the tehsildar of Kazhakkoottam. All my friends had come, in new and beautiful clothes. Though she said so, everyone knows how badly she hated history. But today her being talkative was a big advantage for me. It was time for the execution of the plan. I narrated the whole story in front of them and Gopi started laughing, but Bhola was very serious, as he was expected to be. He said, "Gopi, are you laughing? Seriously?" As he said this, Gopi turned silent. She then said, "You tell me what to do? The people of the village are scared of the dead history master, I am scared of the one who is still alive and teaching me daily!" Bhola continued, "Don't you think that this village needs a change? We are the future of our nation and we should be the ones to open the eyes of our people. We should bust this myth, what do you say Robin?" "But who will go?" He quickly replied, "I will go!" Gopi and Bhola were cordially invited, as they are my best friends. After having the food, we decided to have some fun. Gopi is the most talkative girl of our class, but today she was talking at a different pace. She was explaining her relations with the most popular subject of our school, HISTORY! She said, "Oh my Goodness! How I wonder can there be any subject as boring as history? What’s really the point of learning something which is of no use in the present?" I argued, as a part of the plan, “But, Gopi, we learn from our roots, our past…” “I am not opposing that, buddy, but what do you learn from that boring master. He teaches history as if he has to rush somewhere by the train in the morning, I mean it doesn’t feel like learning. History should be taught like a story, like a drama, like an emotion, like a tale, like a…” And that was what I wanted. I warned him, actually just acting like I was warning him, "But Bhola, Appa was saying that whoever goes inside, never comes back. Please don't leave us alone!" Bhola, as he was expected to be, neglected the warning, and, acting like a hero, spoke a very heavy dialogue, "Why to fear, when Bholaram Rao is here!" And he jumped and dashed towards the school. I gave a loud clap to Gopi and both of us went to our homes. Well, I am so excited about tomorrow. What will happen next is so much awaited. Bhola is the most innocent child of my age. He is the only person who acts as he is expected to. I am way too excited to see how brave he is. Robin 25 March 2015 Dear Diary, Do you know what happened today? As soon as I came out in the morning, Appa called me with an angry voice, "Purushottam!" After hearing 'Purushottam' (my full name), instead of 'Robin', my excitedness dropped suddenly from its peak to as deep as the Mariana Trench. I went out and the only thing I thought of was, no matter what Appa asked me, I just have to answer with a simple no. But, for me it was a true adventure, and adventures are not that easy. "Tell me where is Bhola?" Appa asked, in a super angry mood. And before I heard it, I started crying, "Appa, I have not done anything. Trust me, I am your only child. It was he himself who went to that haunted school!" The moment I said HAUNTED SCHOOL, Appa immediately shouted, "Purushottam, do you even know what you have done? You didn’t even think of the prestige of your father. Are you no more scared of my rage? Your mother has always shielded you from me and my rage, that is the only reason for your mischiefs increasing consistently. Do you know what happened last night? All of us heard Bhola's scream. His father has come to me begging to help him find Bhola." And then Appa and Rao uncle ran towards the school. Gopi and I also decided to follow them. What we found was even more hilarious than the gossips of Amma and the neighbours. Bhola was lying on ground, in the backyard of the school, with his pant tucked at the branch of the tree. He was snoring and sleeping! We took him and came back to my house. When Amma made him drink some water, he woke up, screaming, "Please don't eat me, not me. I am a small child. I love history. Please leave me." Then, after a little while, he calmed and narrated the whole story. Last night, when he reached the school, he lit a lamp and proceeded further. He didn't find anything except dry leaves and old stuff. When he was returning from the backyard, he felt as if someone held his pant and he screamed as loud as he could. Then the lamp fell from his hands, his legs jumped out of his pants, and he lay on the ground, unconscious. Then all of us laughed louder than ever before. Appa said, "You see Mr. Rao, this was the ghost of our history teacher, the tree in the backyard!" So once again, Gopi, I, and our innocent buddy Bhola, busted this myth and were praised for our bravery. Now, maybe I will visit the school again and this time, flee with my friends to nature’s masterpiece. That was how my adventure ended, this time, after solving the age-old mystery of the ghost of the history teacher. Let's see what tomorrow unfolds for me! level_3.title: The dark night
level_3.Text: It was a dark night and everyone knew that I am afraid of the dark. Amma says " I should fight with dark ". Always she says and I listen. Slowly, I removed my blanket and I saw some eyes were watching me. Suddenly those eyes started to move over my head. I got frightened of them. While watching it DHADAMMMMMM....... I fell down and saw now, the big eyes were watching me. "What is it?" I asked myself. Slowly Slowly, I crawled towards to touch those eyes. OHH!!! these were fireflies. Those big eyes were two fireflies's light. The pair was dancing and I was able to listen the clear sound BIZZZZZZZ........... Now room was full of fireflies and I was enjoying it with them. I realized that I have made new friends to get relief from the dark and I was comfortable with them. I don't get afraid anymore now. I can go anywhere in the dark with my different friends.

level_3.title: The Journey From A Novice To A Veteran Archer
level_3.Text: Chapter 1: The Beginning The story starts in a small cottage with a poor boy, named Jon, actually, Jon was not an ordinary boy and he had long hair too. In school, he was called a pitiful, fat loser, because of his effeminate habits and poor situations. As one day, he was walking down from school to his home, he thought if he could change his reputation. Just before he got home his mother was sobbing and he asked "Mother...", and just then his sister Lydia came and yelled "Oh brother, are you mad, can't you just look at her and discover what had happened?", Jon then too shouted, "Are you a termagant, you're always screaming and howling here and there." After a while, Jon tried to control his temper and poped the question, "What happened my mother dear?", his mother replied, "Oh, my son, what should I tell you, we are turning insolvent. We have no money left, your father is also foiled with his crops.". This moment, Jon was kept in a self-made seclusion. (May fate decide...) Chapter 2: The Ultimate Opinion and View As a non-fatalist, Jon was on his reasoning, he didn't believe in bin fate. As he was on his way to the market, he mused, "What can I do so that I can gain a living, switch my effeminate reputation and take the place of a real, consonant man?". Next off, he saw a man making fat, hard money by shooting bullseyes with bow and arrow. He got the clue of becoming an archer, he kept a word of honour to give his blood and sweat to become a legend, he told the troth to his mother and went to the market to find his equipment and tools. (Look what did he find in the next chapter.) Chapter 3: Vow To Become When Jon found a bow and arrow, he went home to practise. He developed and indefatigable attitude towards archery, as days passed, now he wanted to aim real things so he bought fruits and vegetables. First of all, he tried to aim the watermelon. When the arrow dragged towards the target, the watermelon and all eatables came alive and said: "You are a loser aren't you, and you're trying to aim at us? Ha Ha Ha...". When they were trying to make fun of him, he raged with anger and set his aim. He showed up his arrow and shot it in the sky, vowing "I take the pledge that, I may become history's greatest archer & be the cynosure for every eye. I will destroy all sadists and evildoer, and always stake my life to save the world and humanity, I may always stop the world from going into wrong and deadly hands." (What would happen next?") Chapter 4: Writing a Saga Just when the arrow reached the sky, a lightning thunder flashed through his eyes, Jon was literally amazed! An unknown, mysterious voice came "You may come to me and I will train you.", and just before him a pair of stairs appeared. When he climbed up the stairs, a holy God came to him. He taught Jon for years and years, until one day, Jon returned as an invincible, invulnerable warrior, though he was an almighty, he didn't boast of his power instead he became an ascetic, altruistic samaritan to help mankind. Later, Jon became the only rescuer and protector of the people, he gained the respect of a versatile hero of all time. However, we all know that a moment of happiness doesn't last forever, and a disaster occurred. A demon wanted to put an end to earth and humankind. When Jon went to convince him, he threw him out and refused. So Jon was forced to battle and the battle took months to end but at the last Jon was stabbed with a knife. After the battle ended, the demon gave up but a tragedy also had taken place. Just after the terrible battle, the mayor of the city made a statue of Jon with his bow in his memorial, appreciating him as a veteran archer and martyr for all. - Anant Deep Agrawal THE MORAL OF THE STORY The starting point of all achievements is "DESIRE" The stronger the desire, The greater, happy the motivation, The stronger the motivation, the greater the achievement. If You want to achieve something in your life and you desire for that then you can achieve it through hard work and dedication. The next time you're feeling scared or depressed always think of Jon, from him you can always learn about a burning vow and desire.

level_3.title: The Garbage Monster
level_3.Text: Once upon a time there was a boy named Raja. He along with his friends used to make their surroundings very dirty. They used to pluck plants and throw things here and there. One day while playing they came to a deserted place. There were no people and the trees were hardly visible. The place was covered with thorny bushes and a big dump of garbage. As they moved forward they all saw a big black shadow coming out of it. They all were terrified when the shadow started speaking. "I am the Garbage Monster" it said, laughing loudly. You have created me by cutting down trees and dumping waste on Mother Earth and creating concrete jungles. A ll the kids were speechless and in shame and started pleading him to leave them and promised that this time they would do every possible thing to save their Mother Earth. It was then that Raja heard his mother's voice, "Wakeup Raja, It's time to get ready for school". Rubbing his eyes, he got up. He felt that his dream was a lot like reality. It was scary, he witnessed the effects of dumping waste and polluting surroundings. Raja went to the school and told his friends and class teacher about the dream. That is when they all took a pledge: "We would save the environment by planting more trees and not cutting them. Not wasting water, not use plastic bags and no littering. Educate everyone in the society to follow the same." Raja went to the school and told his friends and class teacher about the dream. That is when they all took a pledge: "We would save the environment by planting more trees and not cutting them. Not wasting water, not use plastic bags and no littering. Educate everyone in the society to follow the same."

level_3.title: An ungrateful goldsmith
level_3.Text: Once, there was a traveller named Sushant Hari Singh. He was travelling with a flock of bananas in his bullock cart. It is because in his village, there was no one to purchase his bananas. Therefore, he had to go to the cooperative society by crossing the nearby dense forest. On the way, many bananas fell and nearby monkeys and other animals fought for these bananas. He was often scared of which animal would attack him. He had two bullocks which were enough strong. So, he had nothing to worry. On the way, as he was passing near a well, he heard someone shouting "Help! Help! Someone, please help us! We are not able to live here! This is really suffocating! I think we are going to die here!" Sushant Hari Singh hearing this, pitied and ran in horror to see who was there in the well. When he peeped inside the well, he saw four organisms: A tiger, A monkey, A snake and a man. Sushant Hari Singh immediately put a rope inside the well. After quite a tussle, all the three organisms finally came out except the man. When Sushant tried to rescue that man, the animals, "Oh! Sushant! Don't rescue that man! He is sure to be very ungrateful to you!" But Sushant Hari Singh didn't listen to the animals. He rescued the man too. The man introduced himself as a goldsmith. Goldsmith: Oh! What's your name? Sushant: Oh! My name is Sringeri Srinivas. I am a banana trader. Nice to meet you! Goldsmith: I am a goldsmith. My name is Nanda. I work in the nearby dynasty of Yaravis. Sushant: Oh! Nice to meet you. I hope that Goldsmith: I am your friend. When you are in trouble, you can ask me for your help. Sushant continued on his way. After sometime, he felt tired and decided to take rest. Unfortunately, in that same forest, there was a gang of robbers. They saw him resting. They quickly stopped him, showed him guns, knives and sickles and ordered him to give all the bananas. Sushant refused. The robbers immediately robbed him, tied him and threw him from a cliff top. Sushant fell with a thud. The robbers stole his cart of bananas and his two bullocks. The night had fallen. Sushant was still crying and howling with pain. After sometime, there was a monkey which saw him from a nearby tree. This was the monkey which he had helped when it fall with the rest of the animals. The monkey immediately came down and removed the rope, picked him up and asked him to follow him up. The monkey took him up the hill and made him rest there. The monkey then went to the camp where robbers were fast asleep. It then took all the bananas which were stolen by the robbers. Sushant ate it to the heart's content. The next day, when the robbers woke up, they find all their treasure empty. They foolishly feared that some devil had come. And so, with the bullocks they ran off never to be seen again. Sushant continued on his journey. Later, a tiger called him up from a distance. He feared the tiger but he recalled that it was the tiger whom he had helped when it fell in the well. He went to the tiger's den. As a token of gift, it offered him some food and also gave him a precious golden necklace!!!!!! Sushant Hari Singh took the necklace, thanked the tiger and continued on his way. He then made a decision to pay a visit to the goldsmith whom he had helped. He at last reached the goldsmith's house and the goldsmith welcomed him. Sushant sold some bananas which he had recovered with the help of monkey which in return he got some gold coins. The goldsmith accidently saw the gold necklace in Sushant's hand which the tiger had given to him. The necklace was actually a Xerox copy of the necklace of the princess of the Yaravi king. The goldsmith instead of inquiring him about the necklace, made a wicked plan to somehow captivate Sushant. And so did the goldsmith. When Sushant went to the kitchen to drink some water, the goldsmith immediately took the necklace, ran to the king's palace and complained that Sushant had robbed the necklace of the princess and handed it over to the king. The king immediately sent the guards to the goldsmith's house and Sushant was arrested and put behind the bars even though it was not his mistake. He felt it was illegal to arrest an innocent. But what to do? Even before he could speak the word, the king arrested him. It was the ungratefulness of the goldsmith. The wicked goldsmith thought "Yes!! Now that Sushant is arrested. All his property is now mine!!" And so, Sushant continued to be in sorrow and had to eat whatever was given to him in the jail. Sometimes, he had to go on fast. His family too was sorrowful hearing this incident. All his banana trade stopped. Who helped him at that time? Yes, you are right. It is the snake. It came trough as small hole in the wall of the jail. Sushant at first was scared but later realised it was the snake which he had rescued from the well. The snake had also brought a medicinal herb with him. It gave the medicinal herb to Sushant Hari Singh and said to him that it would go and bite the queen and he should prepare a medicine out of this herb and give it to the queen. Only then, she would recover or else, she was sure to die. And so, the snake unnoticed quietly crept into the room and bit the queen. The queen shouted and yelled. The servants hearing her shout, came running to her room, only to find her fallen on the floor as if she passed away. They saw this snake. They tried to kill it but it escaped from their eyes. Unsuccessful, the servants reported about the queen's snake bite to the king. The king heard this and almost fainted. In that 1 hour time, he consulted many great and excelled physicians but they too were unsuccessful. Finally, when Sushant heard of this, it was now his opportunity to make the king happy and free himself from the jail. He requested the guards to allow him and told them that he had a medicine to cure the queen and so he was let out. Sushant approached and said that he would cure the queen. The king could not believe his eyes. But still, he gave an opportunity to do so. Sushant took the herb to get its juice. This juice was nothing but the venom of that snake. He then applied it to the place where the snake had bit the queen. In no time, the queen regained her consciousness and came back alive. The king felt really happy. He rewarded Sushant with a 1000 gold coins. Sushant could not control his joy that he was released from the jail. When the king enquired about the necklace, Sushant asked where the princess. The king called for the princess. The princess came and in her neck was the same necklace which the goldsmith had shown. The king realized that the necklace which was handed over to the king by the goldsmith was a duplicate necklace. He came to know that the goldsmith was a fraud. He sent his guards to arrest the goldsmith. Sushant Hari Singh took the king's leave and left. Meanwhile, the goldsmith was standing in a railway station waiting for the train. He thought that he was the king's favourite. The guards who were sent by the king finally found the goldsmith, who was trying to board the train and arrested him, and he was put in the jail for lifetime. ﻿Moral: Never be ungrateful to anyone.
